historical_references.reference: Fahim ibn Abi Hajl al-Kufi, a prominent scholar of the early Abbasid period (750-827 AD). He was known for his expertise in hadith and fiqh and was a teacher of many notable scholars including Abu Hanifah and Ibrahim al-Nakid. He was also a prolific author and wrote numerous books on various topics including the science of Qira'ah (recitation of the Quran) and the science of Hadith.
historical_references.context: A prominent scholar of hadith and fiqh in the early Abbasid era, teacher of notable scholars and prolific author.

historical_references.reference: Al-Fahim ibn Ibrahim al-Juwayni, a renowned scholar of the Saljuq period (1037-1118 AD). He was a Hanafi jurist and theologian who served as the chief judge of Nishapur under the Saljuq ruler, Sanjar. He was also a prolific writer and his most famous work is 'Al-Burhan fi Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah', an influential work in Sunni theology.
historical_references.context: A Hanafi jurist and theologian during the Saljuq era, who served as the chief judge of Nishapur and wrote an influential work in Sunni theology.
